cards.text: The LORD has been telling Moses, Israel's leader, about the offerings (Leviticus 1:1-6:7). Now He gives Moses the law for each one, to command Aaron and his sons, the priests. First up is the burnt offering, and it stays on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning.

cards.question: The burnt offering stays on the altar all night. What does God say about the altar fire?

answers.text: It must be put out at night
It must be lit fresh each morning

cards.text: The priest puts on his linen robe and linen undergarments, removes the ashes from the altar and places them beside it, then changes into other clothes and carries the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place. Every morning he adds wood, arranges the burnt offering and burns the fat portions of the peace offerings, and the fire must not be extinguished. No snooze button on THAT job, friend.
Next comes the law of the grain offering. The priest takes a handful of the fine flour and oil, with all the frankincense, and burns it on the altar as the memorial portion.

cards.question: Why does the priest burn that handful of the grain offering on the altar?

answers.text: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD
To pay what the giver owes
To keep the altar fire going

cards.question: Once that handful is burned, Aaron and his sons ___ the rest of the grain offering.

cards.text: They eat it without leaven in a holy place, the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting, and God says, "I have assigned it as their portion of My food offerings." Any male among Aaron's sons may eat it, a permanent portion for the generations to come. A share with their name on it for GENERATIONS, friend, and most of us can't hold on to a reserved parking spot for a week.

Then the LORD tells Moses about the grain offering Aaron and his sons present on the day he is anointed, half in the morning and half in the evening. Fine flour, oil, a griddle, well-kneaded, broken in pieces: friend, NOW you're speaking my language.

cards.question: The priests get to eat most grain offerings. But what happens to every grain offering for a priest?

answers.text: It is eaten by the high priest
It is shared with the people

cards.text: Next comes the law of the sin offering, and it is most holy. It's slaughtered before the LORD in the same place the burnt offering is slaughtered.

cards.question: True or false: The priest who offers the sin offering eats it.

cards.text: The priest eats it in a holy place, the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting, and anything that touches its flesh will become holy. Blood spattered on a garment is washed in a holy place, a clay pot it's boiled in must be broken, and a bronze pot must be scoured and rinsed with water. Any male among the priests may eat it, and it is most holy.

cards.question: True or false: A sin offering may still be eaten even if its blood was brought into the Holy Place to make atonement.

cards.text: The LORD is still giving Moses the law of each offering for the priests, and now it's the guilt offering, which is most holy. It's slaughtered where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the priest splatters its blood on all sides of the altar, and he burns all its fat on the altar as a food offering to the LORD.

cards.question: God says the guilt offering is like the ___ offering, and the same law applies to both.

cards.text: Then God spells out what the priests keep. The hide of a burnt offering goes to the priest who presents it, and so does any grain offering baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle, while every grain offering that's dry or mixed with oil belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron. Back when I sat on a family's kitchen counter, my cut of every batch was the dough stuck in my lines.

Next comes the law of the peace offering. If someone offers it in thanksgiving, he brings unleavened cakes, unleavened wafers, cakes of fine flour and cakes of leavened bread with it, and one portion of each goes to the priest who sprinkles the blood. The thanksgiving meat must be eaten the day it's offered, a vow or a freewill offering may be finished the next day, and anything left on the third day must be burned up. In my bakery, cookies don't make it to morning either, but that's mostly because of me.

cards.question: True or false: If any meat from a peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will still be accepted.

cards.text: Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten, so it gets burned up. Any other meat, anyone who is ceremonially clean may eat.

cards.question: What happens to someone who is unclean and eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD?

answers.text: That person is cut off from his people
That person must pay back a fifth more
That person must wash and wait till evening

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, and this time it's about the fat of an ox, a sheep or a goat.

cards.question: Who does the LORD tell Moses to give this command about the fat to?

cards.text: The Israelites are not to eat any of that fat, and fat from an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts may be used for other things but never eaten. They must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of their dwellings either. Anyone who eats the fat of an animal fit for a food offering to the LORD, or eats blood, must be cut off from his people.
Back to the peace offering, and who gets what. The one bringing it carries the fat and the breast with his own hands, and waves the breast as a wave offering before the LORD.

cards.question: The priest burns the fat of the peace offering on the altar. Who gets the breast that was waved?
True or false: The right thigh of the peace offering goes to the priest who presents its blood and fat.

cards.text: God says He has taken the breast and the thigh from the sons of Israel and given them to Aaron and his sons as a permanent portion. It's been their portion since the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests, and on the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded the sons of Israel to give it to them.
And that's the law of the burnt, grain, sin, guilt, ordination and peace offerings.

cards.question: The LORD gave Moses all these laws on Mount Sinai. That day, what did He command the Israelites to do?

answers.text: Present their offerings to the LORD
